cold_email.subject: Interest in Training Coordinator — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear eClerx Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Training Coordinator opportunity with eClerx at eClerx.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Student Accounts Specialist — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear University of Portland Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Student Accounts Specialist opportunity with University of Portland at University of Portland.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Entry-Level Appointment Coordinator - Training Provided (Centennial) / $65,000-$95,000 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear The Dorne Region Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Entry-Level Appointment Coordinator - Training Provided (Centennial) / $65,000-$95,000 opportunity with The Dorne Region at The Dorne Region.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Behavior Analyst Administrative Assistant — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Restore Hyper Wellness Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Behavior Analyst Administrative Assistant opportunity with Restore Hyper Wellness at Restore Hyper Wellness.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Operations Associate, University of Texas, #1630 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Gopuff Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Operations Associate, University of Texas, #1630 opportunity with Gopuff at Gopuff.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Operations Associate, University Park, #602 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Gopuff Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Operations Associate, University Park, #602 opportunity with Gopuff at Gopuff.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. cold_email.subject: Interest in Operations Associate, University Hills, #478 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Gopuff Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Operations Associate, University Hills, #478 opportunity with Gopuff at Gopuff.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in English Language Development Teacher - ELEVATE/ACE (Accelerating Campus Excellence) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Fort Worth ISD Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the English Language Development Teacher - ELEVATE/ACE (Accelerating Campus Excellence) opportunity with Fort Worth ISD at Fort Worth ISD.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Entry Level Test Systems Engineer (University of Michigan 2026) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear DMC Engineering Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Entry Level Test Systems Engineer (University of Michigan 2026) opportunity with DMC Engineering at DMC Engineering.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Client Service Coordinator — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Banfield Pet Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Client Service Coordinator opportunity with Banfield Pet Hospital at Banfield Pet Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Client Service Coordinator - 002065 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Banfield Pet Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Client Service Coordinator - 002065 opportunity with Banfield Pet Hospital at Banfield Pet Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Westerville Client Service Coordinator — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Banfield Pet Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Westerville Client Service Coordinator opportunity with Banfield Pet Hospital at Banfield Pet Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Research Associate I – Brain Proteome Organization — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Allen Institute Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Associate I – Brain Proteome Organization opportunity with Allen Institute at Allen Institute.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

Dear University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Coordinator, Human Resources and Operations opportunity with University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science at University of Maryland Center for Environmental Science.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Associate Scientist - Robotics & Automation, Vaccines
jobs.location: United States - New York - Pearl River
jobs.description: Use Your Power for Purpose At Pfizer, our purpose is to deliver breakthroughs that transform patients' lives. Central to this mission is our Research and Development team, which strives to convert advanced science and cutting-edge technologies into impactful therapies and vaccines. Whether you are engaged in discovery sciences, ensuring drug safety and efficacy, or supporting clinical trials, your role is crucial. You will leverage innovative design and process development capabilities to expedite the delivery of top tier medicines to patients globally. By integrating advanced scientific knowledge with practical applications, we aim to bring the most effective treatments to those in need, fulfilling our commitment to improving health outcomes worldwide. What Will Be Achieved The Associate Scientist in the Clinical Immunology & Diagnostics, Robotics & Automation group supports Pfizer's vaccine research portfolio through the execution of automated sample preparation workflows. The role utilizes advanced laboratory automation systems to generate high-quality assay-ready materials, while ensuring high standards of compliance and operational excellence. How It Will Be Achieved Operate, monitor, troubleshoot, and maintain laboratory automation systems to ensure reliable, compliant, and efficient laboratory operations. Follow approved procedures, safety requirements, and quality standards while seeking guidance as appropriate to ensure successful execution of assigned responsibilities. Execute assigned work and responsibilities to meet schedule demands, project milestones, and operational deadlines while maintaining a high standard of quality. Support the management of laboratory materials, reagents, controls, reference standards, and consumables required for automated workflows. Collaborate effectively with scientific, operational, and quality partners to support laboratory objectives and project deliverables. Maintain current departmental, quality and safety training requirements. Minimum Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Biology, Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Engineering, or a related scientific field. Experience working in a laboratory, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or academic environment. Strong troubleshooting, analytical, and problem-solving skills. Excellent attention to detail and organizational skills. Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Verbal and written communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across cross-functional teams. Proficiency with Microsoft Office and electronic laboratory systems. Experience using common AI tools, including generative technologies such as ChatGPT or Microsoft Copilot, to support problem solving and enhance productivity. Demonstrated curiosity for exploring how these tools can improve outcomes and understanding of responsible AI practices, including risk management and ethical use. Preferred Qualifications: Experience with laboratory automation, robotic liquid handling platforms (e.g., Hamilton, Tecan, Beckman Coulter), and high-throughput sample preparation workflows. Knowledge of regulated laboratory practices, data integrity principles, and quality systems (e.g., GxP). Familiarity with common AI-enabled tools to support problem solving and enhance productivity. PHYSICAL/MENTAL REQUIREMENTS This position requires significant time in a laboratory environment and the ability to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE). Ability to lift up to 50 pounds and perform activities such as standing, walking, bending, reaching, and sitting for extended periods while working at laboratory workstations, automation platforms, and computer workstations. Ability to analyze data and apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills to support laboratory operations and process improvements. NON-STANDARD WORK SCHEDULE, TRAVEL OR ENVIRONMENT REQUIREMENTS This position may require occasional evening and weekend work to support laboratory operations and meet critical project timelines and business needs. Work Location Assignment: On Premise The annual base salary for this position ranges from $60,200.00 to $100,400.00. In addition, this position is eligible for participation in Pfizer’s Global Performance Plan with a bonus target of 7.5% of the base salary. We offer comprehensive and generous benefits and programs to help our colleagues lead healthy lives and to support each of life’s moments. Benefits offered include a 401(k) plan with Pfizer Matching Contributions and an additional Pfizer Retirement Savings Contribution, paid vacation, holiday and personal days, paid caregiver/parental and medical leave, and health benefits to include medical, prescription drug, dental and vision coverage. Learn more at Pfizer Candidate Site – U.S. Benefits | (uscandidates.mypfizerbenefits.com). Pfizer compensation structures and benefit packages are aligned based on the location of hire. The United States salary range provided does not apply to Tampa, FL or any location outside of the United States. Relocation assistance may be available based on business needs and/or eligibility. Candidates must be authorized to be employed in the U.S. by any employer. U.S. work visa sponsorship (such as TN, O-1, H-1B, etc.) is not available for this role now or in the future. These laws and regulations require Pfizer to provide government agencies with information such as a health care provider’s name, address and the type of payments or other value received, generally for public disclosure. Subject to further legal review and statutory or regulatory clarification, which Pfizer intends to pursue, reimbursement of recruiting expenses for licensed physicians may constitute a reportable transfer of value under the federal transparency law commonly known as the Sunshine Act. Therefore, if you are a licensed physician who incurs recruiting expenses as a result of interviewing with Pfizer that we pay or reimburse, your name, address and the amount of payments made currently will be reported to the government. cold_email.subject: Interest in Associate Scientist - Robotics & Automation, Vaccines — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Pfizer Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Associate Scientist - Robotics & Automation, Vaccines opportunity with Pfizer at Pfizer.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer (Data and Digital Catalyst)
jobs.description: We advance science so that we all have more time with the people we love. A healthier future. It’s what drives us to innovate. To continuously advance science and ensure everyone has access to the healthcare they need today and for generations to come. Creating a world where we all have more time with the people we love. That’s what makes us Roche. Advances in AI, data, and computational sciences are transforming drug discovery and development. Roche’s Research and Early Development organisations at Genentech (gRED) and Pharma (pRED) have demonstrated how these technologies accelerate R&D, leveraging data and novel computational models to drive impact. Seamless data sharing and access to models across gRED and pRED are essential to maximising these opportunities. The new Computational Sciences Center of Excellence (CoE) is a strategic, unified group whose goal is to harness this transformative power of data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to assist our scientists in both pRED and gRED to deliver more innovative and transformative medicines for patients worldwide. Within the CoE organization, the Data and Digital Catalyst (DDC) organisation drives the modernisation of our computational and data ecosystems and integration of digital technologies across Research and Early Development to enable our stakeholders, power data-driven science and accelerate decision-making. The Engineering - AI Enablement group within DDC is accountable for… enabling AI! We do this across the board with our scientific and computational partners based on their goals. We help embed our AI strategy across our research organizations by providing employees with the tools and support needed to adopt AI into our daily work—helping us work smarter and enhancing our day-to-day work. We also build and deploy AI based solutions that reshape and transform business processes in order to unlock value at scale and optimize workflows. We also work on scaling up model training and inference, evaluating the quality of AI/ML models and output, and building impactful applications which accelerate the scientists doing the critical work of drug discovery and development. Partnering with colleagues to build, deploy and evolve a modern tech stack and utilities to enable our AI/ML and agentic efforts will be a key foundation to our success. Our aim is for everyone who can benefit from AI/ML to be able to leverage that utility where and when they need it, from data analysis to literature search to documentation writing. We are aiming for AI/ML to be an everyday utility. The team is cross-functional, impact driven, independent, and constantly evolving to meet the scientific needs. The Opportunity: As a machine learning engineer in AI Enablement, you will be working closely with folks that span the gamut from Computational Scientists, Research Scientists, AI/ML experts, Product leaders, DevOps, and everyone in between. You'll build, own, and constantly improve scalable AI/ML based systems that unlock the potential of our diverse scientific data, accelerating the discovery and development of life-changing treatments for patients. Design, develop, and test robust, scalable, and maintainable AI/ML facing scientific web applications and backend systems. Build tools to evaluate AI/ML model performance and establish new ways to understand AI quality. Partner with product managers and scientists to understand user needs, shape requirements, and translate them into actionable technical specifications. Develop and maintain systems for collecting, structuring, and storing diverse scientific data that support advanced analytics, machine learning, and other data-driven initiatives. Implement, adopt, or evaluate new AI/ML algorithms and analytical techniques Contribute to architectural decisions, code reviews, and the evolution of our development processes. Be willing to span the stack and contribute where needed, even outside of your core area of expertise. Stay up-to-date with emerging technologies and industry best practices and adopt a culture of continuous learning, collaboration, and curiosity. Who you are: Strong proficiency with AI/ML frameworks, libraries, and toolsets. Expert knowledge of statistics, machine learning theory, and algorithms. Strong knowledge of ML performance optimization, GPU best practices. cold_email.subject: Interest in Machine Learning Engineer (Data and Digital Catalyst) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Genentech / Roche Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Machine Learning Engineer (Data and Digital Catalyst) opportunity with Genentech / Roche at Genentech / Roche.

I am especially interested in building scalable data systems that let research and clinical teams use biological data reliably. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, I have built API-driven and Snakemake-based pipelines, automated SQL workflows, and worked across both scientific and software contexts.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Client Service Coordinator (Part Time) — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Banfield Pet Hospital Hiring Team,

jobs.title: Associate Scientist, Sample Logistics
jobs.location: United States - New York - Pearl River
jobs.description: Use Your Power for Purpose At Pfizer, our purpose is to deliver breakthroughs that transform patients' lives. Central to this mission is our Research and Development team, which strives to convert advanced science and cutting-edge technologies into impactful therapies and vaccines. Whether you are engaged in discovery sciences, ensuring drug safety and efficacy, or supporting clinical trials, your role is crucial. You will leverage innovative design and process development capabilities to expedite the delivery of top tier medicines to patients globally. By integrating advanced scientific knowledge with practical applications, we aim to bring the most effective treatments to those in need, fulfilling our commitment to improving health outcomes worldwide. What You Will Achieve The primary purpose of this job role is to function as a supporting member of the Sample Logistics (SL) operations within Pfizer Vaccine Research and Development (VRD). The incumbent will be responsible for receiving samples from global clinical/study trials according to approved protocols and processes. The individual will participate in all aspects of tracking and documenting the chain of custody of samples. The incumbent’s role will include sample receipt, documentation, storage, tracking, aliquoting, distribution to the testing labs, and sample disposal. The colleague will work in a team setting and will share roles and responsibilities as assigned by the team leader/manager. How You Will Achieve It The incumbent will be required to complete all processes as detailed in Sample Logistics' Standard Operating Procedures. The colleague will perform job responsibilities in compliance with GXP and all other regulatory agency requirements. The candidate will receive samples from clinical trial sites and enter samples into an electronic database management system. Complete clinical lab supply requests, which includes shipping forms, labels, and other lab supplies as needed. Perform sample storage and retrieval using manual freezers and BiOS (automated freezer storage system). Author Laboratory Manuals to support clinical trial site training and operations. Perform manual sample aliquoting and aliquoting using the Hamilton robotic instrument. Ship samples and lab supplies to external and internal testing labs. Assist in the general maintenance of the Hamilton robotic instruments. Participate in the shipment discrepancy resolution process. Complete documentation according to cGMP/GLP and all other regulatory agency requirements and archives documents as per applicable policies. Carry out sample disposal/sample destruction according to regulated policies and procedures Perform other duties as assigned. Here Is What You Need (Minimum Requirements) Bachelor of Science Degree or Bachelor of Arts Degree in a relevant scientific discipline 0-3 years of experience in the pharmaceutical industry Knowledgeable with Microsoft applications including Word Processing, Excel, and PowerPoint - Ability to work in a team setting Experience using common AI tools, including generative technologies such as ChatGPT or Microsoft Copilot, to support problem solving and enhance productivity. Demonstrated curiosity for exploring how these tools can improve outcomes and understanding of responsible AI practices, including risk management and ethical use. Bonus Points If You Have (Preferred Requirements): Pharmaceutical and biotech drug discovery experience Strong problem-solving skills Excellent communication skills Ability to work independently and as part of a team Strong organizational skills Ability to manage multiple tasks and projects simultaneously Experience using common AI tools, including generative technologies such as ChatGPT or Microsoft Copilot PHYSICAL/MENTAL REQUIREMENTS Work in a lab environment for the majority of the workday. Work with various types of bodily fluids. Work with live microorganisms (e.g., S. pneumoniae) . Ability to lift racks/boxes up to 10 lbs. Work Location Assignment: On Premise The annual base salary for this position ranges from $60,200.00 to $100,400.00. In addition, this position is eligible for participation in Pfizer’s Global Performance Plan with a bonus target of 7.5% of the base salary. We offer comprehensive and generous benefits and programs to help our colleagues lead healthy lives and to support each of life’s moments. Benefits offered include a 401(k) plan with Pfizer Matching Contributions and an additional Pfizer Retirement Savings Contribution, paid vacation, holiday and personal days, paid caregiver/parental and medical leave, and health benefits to include medical, prescription drug, dental and vision coverage. Learn more at Pfizer Candidate Site – U.S. Benefits | (uscandidates.mypfizerbenefits.com). Pfizer compensation structures and benefit packages are aligned based on the location of hire. The United States salary range provided does not apply to Tampa, FL or any location outside of the United States. Relocation assistance may be available based on business needs and/or eligibility. Candidates must be authorized to be employed in the U.S. by any employer. U.S. work visa sponsorship (such as TN, O-1, H-1B, etc.) is not available for this role now or in the future. cold_email.subject: Interest in Associate Scientist, Sample Logistics — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Pfizer Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Associate Scientist, Sample Logistics opportunity with Pfizer at Pfizer.

I am especially interested in building scalable data systems that let research and clinical teams use biological data reliably. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, I have built API-driven and Snakemake-based pipelines, automated SQL workflows, and worked across both scientific and software contexts.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: Research Associate
jobs.description: Position Overview: We are seeking a highly motivated and skilled Research Associate I to join our dynamic team in the sample management. In this role, you will be responsible for the management of biological samples, ensuring their integrity, overseeing quality control, and supporting research projects that rely on biological specimens. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in bio sample management, research methodologies, and data analysis, with an interest in contributing to cutting-edge scientific research. Key Responsibilities: Sample Collection and Processing : Oversee the collection, preparation, and processing of biological samples (e.g., blood, tissue, saliva, DNA) in accordance with established protocols and best practices. Maintain proper documentation and labeling of samples, ensuring traceability from collection to storage. Sample Storage and Management : Ensure proper storage conditions (e.g., temperature, humidity) for various types of biological samples, including cryopreservation and ambient storage. Implement inventory management procedures to track and organize samples, utilizing database systems and laboratory management software (e.g., FreezerPro, LabArchives). Ensure the samples are appropriately cataloged and accessible to researchers in a timely manner. Database Management and Data Analysis : Manage and update the sample database, ensuring accuracy and compliance with sample tracking and research needs. Assist in data analysis and reporting, including the creation of sample inventory reports and performance metrics. Collaborate with the research team to retrieve and prepare data for research publications or grant proposals. Regulatory Compliance and Quality Control : Monitor and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, including HIPAA, IRB guidelines, and biorepository-specific SOPs (Standard Operating Procedures). Implement quality control procedures to ensure sample integrity and that all processes meet accreditation standards (e.g., CAP, ISO, CLIA). Assist in preparing for audits and inspections, ensuring documentation and records are up to date. Collaboration with Researchers : Work closely with internal and external research teams to understand sample requirements, providing expert guidance on sample availability, quality, and suitable use. Support researchers by preparing and distributing biological samples for experiments and studies. Provide expertise in biorepository protocols, best practices for sample handling, and troubleshooting of issues related to sample collection or storage. Research Support : Assist in the design and execution of research projects involving the biorepository’s sample collection and management processes. Contribute to scientific publications, presentations, and other research outputs, providing data and insights from biorepository-managed samples. Continuous Improvement and Training : Proactively identify areas for process improvement in sample management and recommend strategies to enhance operational efficiency. Stay current with advancements in biorepository management, biosample storage technology, and related regulatory guidelines. Mentor and train junior staff or technicians on best practices in sample handling and database management. Qualifications: Education : Bachelor’s degree in Biological Sciences, Biotechnology, Molecular Biology, or a related field (preferred). Experience : 0-2 years of experience in a laboratory or biorepository setting, with a focus on sample management, biospecimen processing, and quality assurance. Familiarity with biorepository software and data management tools (e.g., FreezerPro, LabArchives, LabWare, snowflake based database, LIMS, is highly desirable. Skills : Strong understanding of biological sample management, including tissue processing, cryopreservation, DNA/RNA extraction, and cell culture. Knowledge of regulatory compliance (HIPAA, GxP, CLIA, IRB). Proficiency in data analysis and database management (e.g., Excel, SPSS, R). Excellent organizational skills with keen attention to detail and accuracy. Ability to troubleshoot technical issues and provide practical solutions. Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively with researchers and other staff. Experience with laboratory equipment (e.g., freezers, liquid nitrogen tanks, centrifuges) and ensuring proper calibration and maintenance. Experience in SQL, Python Plus. Working Conditions: This position involves working in a controlled laboratory environment with exposure to biological samples, chemicals, and laboratory equipment. Candidates must adhere to strict biosafety protocols and wear appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) as required. An occasional evening, weekend, or holiday hours may be necessary depending on project The pay range is listed and actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. This may differ in other locations due to cost of labor considerations. Austin, TX $61,800 — $77,300 USD OUR OPPORTUNITY Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives. The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. When you join Natera, you’ll work hard and grow quickly. Working alongside the elite of the industry, you’ll be stretched and challenged, and take pride in being part of a company that is changing the landscape of genetic disease management. WHAT WE OFFER Competitive Benefits - Employee benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, vision, life and disability plans for eligible employees and their dependents. Additionally, Natera employees and their immediate families receive free testing in addition to fertility care benefits. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program! jobs.title: Mechanical Engineer, PCBA Test Infrastructure, Robotics
jobs.description: ABOUT THE TEAM Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives. ABOUT THE ROLE We are seeking a Mechanical Engineer for a senior individual-contributor role leading printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) test fixtures and infrastructure for advanced robotic systems. You will independently turn evolving requirements into working fixtures, make technical tradeoffs, and own delivery from concept and detailed design through fabrication, validation, deployment, and reliable operation. This role combines development-lab work with deployment at contract manufacturers. You will build precision mechanical systems for board programming, functional test, and characterization, including board nests, probe plates, connector interfaces, alignment features, clamps, enclosures, and thermal interfaces. You will partner with electrical, firmware, software, manufacturing, and reliability teams to make fixtures repeatable, protective of delicate assemblies, and maintainable as board designs evolve. This role is based in San Francisco, CA, and requires in-person presence 4 days a week. Travel to contract-manufacturer sites is part of the role, with timing based on build and deployment needs. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Own the mechanical architecture of PCBA test stations, including frames, board nests, datum schemes, access, guarding, ergonomics, and serviceability. - Design probe and bed-of-nails fixtures, connector-mating mechanisms, board supports, clamps, and interchangeable tooling for programming, functional test, and characterization. - Use first-principles analysis and simulation to assess stiffness, probe and insertion forces, board deflection, tolerance stacks, thermal growth, and fixture life; validate key predictions on hardware. - Develop locating and compliance features that accommodate board and assembly variation, protect components and solder joints, and preserve contact repeatability across loading cycles and board revisions. - Partner with electrical engineers on test-point access, probe selection, connector engagement, ESD provisions, cable routing, cooling, and interlocks; define motion and sequencing constraints with software and controls partners. - Build, assemble, instrument, and debug fixtures in the lab. Establish acceptance checks for alignment, force, board strain where needed, contact repeatability, and cycle life; separate fixture problems from board failures. - Design safe loading, pinch-point protection, hard stops, and operator access for manual or actuated fixtures. Make wear components easy to inspect, clean, and replace. - Manage fabrication partners and component vendors. Release CAD, drawings, bills of materials, tolerance analyses, assembly instructions, inspection plans, and maintenance procedures. - Own fixture deployment and acceptance at contract manufacturers, including assembly and alignment checks, correlation with lab fixtures, operator training, and troubleshooting. Support replication, board-revision changes, and maintenance through released documentation. YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU: - Have strong mechanical intuition for precision interfaces, load paths, compliance, tolerances, and the behavior of delicate electronic assemblies. - Move readily between analysis, CAD, vendor collaboration, and hands-on assembly and debugging. - Care about repeatable contact, controlled forces, operator usability, and equipment that others can maintain. - Take ownership from concept through reliable daily operation, adapting fixtures to evolving boards and communicating clearly across electrical, software, manufacturing, and operations teams. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS - Demonstrated ability to independently deliver significant precision-fixture or equipment projects from ambiguous requirements through detailed design, fabrication, validation, and sustained use. - Strong 3D CAD and released-drawing capability, including complete fabrication and assembly packages, bills of materials, and revision control. - Strong fundamentals in GD&T, tolerance analysis, locating schemes, stiffness, compliance, contact forces, and load paths. - Hands-on ability to work with fabrication partners, assemble and measure fixtures, diagnose failures, and iterate hardware in a lab or manufacturing environment. - Ability to define and execute fixture acceptance checks for alignment, force, repeatability, wear, and safe operation, using evidence to distinguish fixture problems from product variation. - Ability to communicate interfaces and tradeoffs across electrical, software, manufacturing, and operations teams and support deployment and troubleshooting at contract manufacturers. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS - Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. - Prior PCBA test-fixture experience with board nests, probe or bed-of-nails fixtures, connector mating, and protection of delicate electronic assemblies. - Experience with ESD-aware tooling, thermal interfaces, actuated fixtures, interlocks, or structural and thermal simulation. - Experience with NX, SolidWorks, Creo, or equivalent tools; robotics hardware; or fixture replication and new-product builds at contract manufacturers. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE - Deliver a reusable PCBA fixture that meets agreed alignment, contact, board-support, and loading requirements, with demonstrated repeatability and protection of the assembly under test. - Validate fixture wear and cycle life, identify sources of intermittent contact or board loading, and improve contact-related failures, changeover time, and serviceability against agreed targets. - Deploy and accept the fixture at a contract manufacturer with released CAD, drawings, inspection checks, assembly instructions, spare-parts information, and maintenance procedures that enable others to reproduce and sustain it. jobs.title: Scientist 3, CVRM Discovery Research Biology
jobs.description: The Opportunity A healthier future. It’s what drives us to innovate. To continuously advance science and ensure everyone has access to the healthcare they need today and for generations to come. Creating a world where we all have more time with the people we love. That’s what makes us Genentech. The Cardiovascular, Renal and Metabolism (CVRM) Research Biology group within Genentech Research and Early Development (gRED) is seeking an innovative and highly motivated Scientist 3 to advance our extra-hepatic, cell- and tissue-selective drug delivery platforms. In this laboratory-based role, you will lead the biological discovery and validation of novel cell-surface receptors to enable targeted delivery of nucleic acid therapeutics (such as siRNAs and ASOs). Working in close cross-functional partnership with therapeutic discovery, vector design, proteomics, and disease biology teams, you will directly shape next-generation delivery strategies for CVRM indications. Develop and execute an overarching biological strategy to identify, prioritize, and validate cell-surface receptors capable of mediating selective nucleic acid delivery to CVRM-relevant tissues. Establish, culture, and characterize physiologically relevant in vitro and ex vivo cellular systems (including striated muscle) for targeted-delivery evaluation. Design and implement quantitative mechanistic assays to assess ligand-receptor binding, occupancy, internalization kinetics, intracellular trafficking, and endosomal escape. Evaluate novel targeting ligands and bioconjugates (such as antibody- or peptide-oligonucleotide conjugates) for functional cargo delivery, downstream pharmacodynamics, and target gene modulation. Apply genetic and molecular perturbation tools, including CRISPR and RNAi, alongside biochemical methods to establish definitive receptor dependency and mechanism of action. Design and execute preclinical in vivo biodistribution and proof-of-concept pharmacology studies to demonstrate disease-modifying therapeutic potential. Communicate experimental conclusions and strategic delivery milestones across cross-functional matrix teams and drug discovery committees. Who You Are Hold a PhD in Cell Biology, Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Pharmacology, Physiology, Bioengineering, or a related discipline (or a Master's degree with 6+ years / Bachelor's degree with 8+ years of equivalent relevant industry research experience). Possess deep mechanistic expertise in cell-surface receptor biology, membrane proteins, receptor-mediated endocytosis, and intracellular vesicle trafficking pathways. Demonstrate proven hands-on capability in mammalian cell culture (primary cells, stem-cell-derived lineages, or ex vivo tissues) and quantitative cell-based assay development. Experience with specialized CVRM cellular systems including cardiomyocytes, vascular endothelium, adipose tissue, or skeletal muscle. Demonstrate technical proficiency in molecular biology techniques (CRISPR, RNAi, qRT-PCR/digital PCR, RNAseq, Western blotting, or immunoassays) and cellular analysis tools (flow cytometry or high-content imaging). Possess a documented record of scientific achievement through peer-reviewed publications, patents, or recognized contributions to drug discovery pipelines, complemented by outstanding collaborative and communication skills. Preferred PhD strongly preferred. Direct experience with oligonucleotide therapeutics (siRNA, ASO) and targeted conjugate platforms (e.g., antibody-oligonucleotide conjugates, peptide/ligand conjugates). Deep understanding of mechanisms governing endosomal escape and productive intracellular bioavailability. Hands-on familiarity with cell-surface proteomics ("surfaceomics"), spatial transcriptomics, or single-cell RNA sequencing for target receptor discovery. Practical expertise with quantitative live-cell confocal imaging, high-content imaging platforms, and automated image analysis. Experience with preclinical in vivo biodistribution, pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) studies, and tissue pharmacodynamic profiling. jobs.title: Product Reliability Engineer
jobs.description: About the Team OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops silicon and system-level solutions designed for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. The team is responsible for building the next generation of AI-native silicon while working closely with software and research partners to co-design hardware tightly integrated with AI models. In addition to delivering production-grade silicon for OpenAI’s supercomputing infrastructure, the team also creates custom design tools and methodologies that accelerate innovation and enable hardware optimized specifically for AI. The Compute team works on the design of our AI supercomputers, doing everything from workload modeling to influencing accelerator design. We’re leaning into our partnerships to make system and data center co-design an integral part of this process, and are looking for engineers to design AI supercomputers solutions for data center applications This team is responsible for working with partners to optimize their hardware for our workloads, identifying promising new deep learning accelerators, and bringing those hardware platforms to production. If you’re excited to work at the intersection of cutting edge deep learning, hardware system, and data center design this role is for you! About the Role We’re looking for a Product Reliability Engineer to own reliability engineering for advanced IT hardware, from printed circuit board assemblies (PCBAs) through compute and networking trays, systems, and fully integrated racks. You’ll translate operating conditions and service-life goals into reliability requirements, design and execute qualification tests, and drive failure analysis and corrective-action verification from development through production and field deployment. Working with electrical, mechanical, thermal, manufacturing, quality, and data center teams, suppliers, and manufacturing partners, you’ll use test and field evidence to improve hardware durability, serviceability, and availability. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you will: - Define reliability requirements and targets for PCBAs, trays, systems, and racks using mission profiles, expected service life, operating environments, duty cycles, and availability goals. - Drive design-for-reliability reviews with electrical, mechanical, and thermal engineers. Use failure modes and effects analysis (DFMEA or FMEA) and physics of failure to prioritize risks and recommend design improvements. Own component de-rating guidelines and guidance. - Own reliability qualification plans from new product introduction through production, defining test coverage, representative configurations, sample sizes, stress conditions, duration, pass/fail criteria, and exit evidence at each assembly level. - Develop and execute accelerated life and environmental tests, including temperature cycling, humidity exposure, power cycling, shock, vibration, and transport testing. Exercise hardware under representative workloads and monitor function and degradation during stress. - Analyze life-test and field data using Weibull and other reliability models, acceleration models, and confidence intervals. State assumptions, exposure, and uncertainty when estimating failure rates, useful life, or reliability against targets. - Lead failure investigations from symptom reproduction through physical root cause. Maintain failure reporting, analysis, and corrective-action records, and verify fixes through targeted testing and recurrence monitoring. - Review supplier reliability plans and evidence for PCBs, PCBa components/assemblies, cables, connectors, and cooling components. Identify gaps between component qualification and the stresses encountered in the integrated system or rack. - Work hands-on with internal and partner labs to develop fixtures, instrumentation, and test methods. Review sample traceability, test configurations, calibration, raw data, and failure capture, including on-site support at manufacturing partners. - Partner with manufacturing and quality engineers to establish and validate reliability screens, burn-in where justified, and ongoing reliability testing. Confirm screening detects relevant defects without consuming unacceptable product life. - Evaluate reliability risks introduced by assembly and integration: board strain and solder-joint damage, connector mating and retention, cable routing, fastener preload, power connections, and thermal interfaces. Partner with cooling specialists on leak integrity, material compatibility, corrosion, and cooling performance over life. - Plan reliability test resources, lab capacity, hardware samples, schedules, and dependencies across programs with engineering teams, technical program managers, suppliers, and manufacturing partners. - Present qualification results, unresolved failure modes, and residual risk at design and release reviews. Make evidence-based readiness recommendations and clearly identify test gaps, required follow-up, and decisions for accountable owners. - Assess reliability impact and define targeted requalification for design, component, supplier, manufacturing process, and repair changes, including firmware changes that alter hardware operating stresses. - Track field returns and fleet failure trends with service and data center teams. Correlate telemetry, failure analysis, and configuration history to prioritize corrective actions and feed lessons into future designs and qualification plans. - Validate serviceability and repeated assembly or maintenance operations, including connector mating cycles and component replacement. Work with system engineers to assess how hardware failures, redundancy, and recovery affect rack availability. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have hands-on reliability engineering experience with advanced IT hardware, such as AI/HPC servers, networking equipment, or storage systems, spanning PCBAs, electromechanical assemblies, and integrated racks. - Have designed, instrumented, and executed hardware reliability tests, debugged failures in the lab, and translated results into practical design or process improvements. - Understand failure mechanisms in electronic assemblies, including solder fatigue, PCB and laminate damage, connector wear, corrosion, and thermal or mechanical degradation. - Can turn mission profiles and failure risks into qualification plans, select defensible sample sizes and stress levels, and explain the assumptions and limits of accelerated testing. - Have led reliability qualification through development and production milestones, balancing sample availability, lab capacity, schedule, and the evidence needed for release decisions. - Have worked directly with component suppliers, joint design manufacturers, contract manufacturers, and external test labs to review test methods, resolve failures, and verify corrective actions. - Apply design for reliability, DFMEA, and physics-of-failure methods across electrical, mechanical, and thermal interfaces, and understand how manufacturing, assembly, handling, and repair affect long-term reliability. - Have driven structured failure analysis and corrective action using methods such as 8D, supported by electrical diagnostics, microscopy, X-ray, cross-section analysis, or specialist failure-analysis labs as appropriate. - Can analyze reliability and life-test data, including censored data, Weibull distributions, and confidence bounds, using tools such as Python, R, JMP, or equivalent statistical software. - Bring experience with high-power electronics, dense interconnects, or liquid-cooled hardware, including thermal interfaces, leak integrity, material compatibility, and serviceability. - Communicate technical findings and uncertainty clearly, distinguish verified root cause and corrective-action effectiveness from hypotheses, and prioritize reliability risks when requirements or designs change. jobs.title: 3P Revenue Accounting & Reporting
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role We are looking for a Senior Manager, 3P Revenue Accounting & Reporting to join our Accounting team. You will own revenue recognition, month-end close and reporting for Claude sold through our cloud service provider (CSP) channels: AWS Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI and Microsoft Azure Marketplace. These channels are among the fastest-growing revenue streams at the company. They run on consumption-based, partner-reported data that changes every month. You will be the accounting point of contact for the finance and partner teams at AWS, Google and Microsoft. Internally, you will partner with Finance, FAB, Engineering and business teams to turn partner billing feeds into accurate, auditable revenue. You will also lead the automation of a close that is still heavily manual. If you want to build the financial infrastructure behind a fast-growing AI company, come join us in our mission to build safe, beneficial AI. Key responsibilities Lead the revenue close for cloud service provider Marketplace within a listed company timeline. Prepare and review revenue, revenue-share, reserve journal entries, accruals and true-ups including memos for accounting assessments and judgments. Own balance sheet reconciliations, reserves, and the usage-to-invoice-to-cash bridge. Perform monthly and quarterly flux analysis and prepare flux decks for leadership. Own quarter-end deliverables, including footnote disclosures, flux commentary and presentations to leadership and Corporate Accounting. Serve as the primary contact for external auditors. Review the work of accountants and contractors, set the close calendar, and keep close packages complete and audit-ready. Own monthly and quarterly 3P revenue reporting for leadership and FP&A, by partner, model, product, region and customer. Review partner usage, invoice, disbursement and fraud reports each month, and resolve data issues before close. Serve as the accounting point of contact for the finance, engineering and product teams and drive reporting improvements that support an on-time close. Apply ASC 606 to 3P arrangements, including principal-vs-agent, variable consideration and reseller arrangements. Estimate and document reserves, including credit loss (ASC 326). Assess the accounting for new 3P products, programs and billing changes, partnering with Technical Accounting on complex judgments. Partner with the Engineering teams to automate manual close processes, including SQL-driven workbooks, automated reconciliations and system-generated journal entries. Own 3P SOX controls, including design, documentation, gap remediation and audit evidence. Partner with FP&A, Treasury, AR and business teams on forecasts, cash and partner disputes. Minimum qualifications Have strong ASC 606 knowledge, especially principal-vs-agent, variable consideration, consideration payable to a customer, and consumption-based revenue. Have owned a month-end close with tight deadlines and reviewed journal entries, reconciliations and flux analysis. Have built revenue reporting from large, imperfect third-party data sets and reconciled it to the general ledger. Have managed external partner relationships where you depended on their data, and pushed for fixes. Have strong SQL skills (BigQuery or similar) and experience automating close workbooks or reconciliations. Have designed or operated SOX controls and supported external audits. Communicate clearly with accounting, finance, business and engineering teams. Thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments where processes are still being built. Preferred qualifications Have 10+ years of progressive accounting experience, including 3+ years managing revenue accounting or close teams. A Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance; CPA or equivalent (ACA, ACCA). Big 4 audit experience combined with industry experience at a high-growth tech or SaaS company. Experience with cloud marketplace, reseller or channel revenue (AWS Marketplace, Google Cloud Marketplace, Azure Marketplace). Experience with usage-based and subscription revenue models. Hands-on experience with Workday Financials, NetSuite, Numeric, Hex or similar close and reporting tools. Experience with IPO readiness. Experience using AI tools to automate accounting and reporting work. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $190,000 — $230,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. cold_email.subject: Interest in Analyst III, Global Internal Audit & Assurance (GIA) - IT Audit — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Bristol Myers Squibb Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Analyst III, Global Internal Audit & Assurance (GIA) - IT Audit opportunity with Bristol Myers Squibb at Bristol Myers Squibb.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.
